source: Cemri et al. MAST-Data (Hugging Face dataset mcemri/MAST-Data), my recount
finding: Recounted the released 1642 annotated traces. 1237 traces carry at least one failure mode. Neither paper split (44.2/32.3/23.5 or 41.8/36.9/21.3) is reproduced exactly; the current release gives a third split.
numbers: Share of 5141 mode instances: specification 37.0%, inter-agent 33.3%, verification 29.9%. Share of all 1642 traces with at least one mode in the category: spec 58.1%, inter-agent 53.3%, verification 55.2%. Step repetition (1.3) is on 40.4% of traces (664), not 15.7%. Reasoning-action mismatch 37.1%, no or incomplete verification 37.0%, incorrect verification 40.1%, unaware of termination 26.6%. Human-labelled file has only 19 traces.
limits: The dataset is a later release than the paper (7 frameworks, 8 benchmarks, 5 LLMs); labels appear to be LLM-made at scale. The two paper splits likely count different things (modes vs failed traces) and the release was re-annotated. Treat all MAST percentages as version-dependent.
agent_relevance: Gap 8 closes: cite MAST shares with the version and counting unit. Step repetition and verification gaps each hit about 40% of traces in the current release, so loop and check defences remain the right focus.

finding: On GSM8K-Complex the strongest model fixed the smallest share of its own errors without hints. Weaker models fixed 1.6 to 1.7 times more. The author calls this the accuracy-correction paradox.
numbers: N=500 problems per model, temperature 0. Accuracy: DeepSeek-Chat 94.0%, GPT-3.5 66.4%, Claude-3-Haiku 70.4%. Intrinsic correction: 16.7% (5/30), 26.8% (45/168), 29.1% (43/148). Detection of own error: 56.7%, 81.5%, 10.1%. Model-made hint: 26.7%, 15.5%, 12.8%. Up to 3 rounds: 20.0%, 67.9%, 60.8%.
limits: Only 3 models, only math word problems, only 30 errors for DeepSeek. Paper text and table disagree on accuracy (68 vs 66.4, 73.3 vs 70.4). Error types self-labelled. Models are old (not reasoning models).
agent_relevance: Fewer errors left means less to fix; a revise step on a strong model has a small upside and a real downside. Supports triggering S5 only when an error is located.

source: Thought-ICS: localise the first wrong step then backtrack (arXiv 2602.02416)
finding: Blind self-verification breaks about as many right answers as it fixes. Locating the first wrong step and resampling from the clean prefix gave a small net gain with no oracle, and a large one with an oracle flag.
numbers: 8 open models 3B to 120B, 6 datasets (AMC23 40 problems, others 100 sampled). Self-verification single: breaks 10.9% of correct, fixes 6.2% of wrong; any-vote: breaks 21.4%, fixes 8.1%; unanimous: breaks 6.0%, fixes 3.5%. Autonomous Thought-ICS-A with confidence safeguard: net +3.9% (2.5% correct broken, 6.4% wrong fixed); without safeguard -49.3% (V/L disagreement exit) and -72.0% (max-iteration exit). Oracle-verified lift 20 to 40%. Clean prefix before true first error in 60 to 80% of localisations vs 30 to 45% for unstructured CoT; resampling from a clean prefix 2 to 4 times better. Reference step labels from 3 frontier models, unanimous on only 51%.
limits: Open models up to 120B; math, science, commonsense with checkable answers. Authors note it is unclear if gains are structured resampling rather than correction. No frontier reasoning models. Only the first 100k characters of the page were read.
agent_relevance: Direct support for the schema choice: S5 revise should name the failing step, and an exit rule that stops when verification is confident protects correct answers. Without the safeguard the loop destroys accuracy.

source: Sentry: learning to recover from LLM agent failures at test time (arXiv 2610.02994)
finding: A failure layer outside the agent detects repeated or stalled actions, retrieves a matching lesson, checks recovery, and stores the lesson only if recovery worked. It beat rule-based and reflection baselines on four benchmarks.
numbers: Qwen3.5-9B agent, 5 runs. WebShop reward: base 0.170, AgentGuard (rule-based) 0.258, AgentFixer 0.171, Sentry 0.468. AppWorld pass: base 25.59, AgentGuard 25.09, Sentry 38.53. SWE-bench Lite: base 0.20, Sentry 0.30. Mind2Web Replay: base 0.420, AgentFixer 0.687, Sentry 0.736. Tokens 1.54x base vs 2.44x for AgentForesight. Local recovery on 200 paired forks 33.5% without intervention vs 60.5% with. GPT-OSS-120B WebShop 0.531.
limits: Same model is agent, detector and verifier. Authors' own benchmark setup. Gains are relative to a weak base (WebShop 0.17). Preprint, no independent replication.
agent_relevance: Closest published test of a Woods-style monitor, respond, learn layer on an LLM agent. It changes behaviour at about 1.5x tokens. Shows an external trigger plus a stored lesson beats reflection in context.

source: Sentry: detector evidence, rule-based baseline and over-triggering (arXiv 2610.02994, appendix and ablations)
finding: Sentry's detector is an LLM call, not code. No ablation compares an LLM detector with a rule-based one inside Sentry. The rule-based AgentGuard baseline (same action 3 times, no-progress rate above 0.75) helped on WebShop and did nothing on AppWorld. A gate that decides whether to intervene mattered most.
numbers: AgentGuard vs base: WebShop 0.258 vs 0.170 (+52%), AppWorld 25.09 vs 25.59 (no gain), SWE-bench 0.22 vs 0.20. Removing Sentry's intervention-need check: WebShop 0.468 to 0.136, AppWorld 38.53 to 23.70; interventions rose 227 to 347 and 187 to 310; guidance lift turned negative (-0.035, -2.05). Recovery by failure type over 939 detected failures: action validity 92.6%, reasoning and grounding 70.2%, progress (repetition or stall) 64.0%, overall 81.7%; SWE-bench progress recovery 34.0%. Human audit 86.0% agreement over 200 windows, kappa 0.82 to 0.89.
limits: Baselines are different systems, not controlled ablations; detector precision and recall not reported. Last 36k characters of the page not read.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 stays open. Rule triggers give modest or zero gain; an unnecessary intervention hurts. Fire rate and change rate on our own traces remain the needed test. Progress failures (our impasse type) are the hardest to recover (64%, 34% on code).

source: What does a repair agent gain from remembering its failure? (arXiv 2610.41433)
finding: A predeclared-contrast test on real Python bugs: remembering the previous failed attempt raised resolve rate by 5 to 10 points but no result was significant after correction. A model-written lesson did not beat the raw transcript it summarises.
numbers: 75 BugsInPy bugs, 181 failed gpt-5.4-mini attempts retried. Plain retry 29.8%. HISTORY +9.4 [-0.5,+18.9], REFLECT (lesson) +7.2 [-2.3,+17.4], SIGNAL +5.5, BOTH +9.9 [+1.5,+19.1] (Holm p 0.17). Lesson minus transcript -1.7 [-8.7,+4.9]. Replication gpt-5.4, 85 failures: plain 43.5%, HISTORY +10.6 [-8.9,+29.3]; edited-a-file rate +14.1 [+5.1,+24.1]. Notice-only control +3.2 / -7.1. Only 1 of 12 predeclared contrasts significant (transcript vs notice, +12.2). Suite-clean gains shrink to +5.0, +2.2, +2.8. Intra-class correlation 0.40; a 7-point effect needs about 106 to 210 tasks.
limits: Same 75 tasks throughout: it tests transfer to a stronger model, not to new tasks. 62 of 181 failures from one project. Small budget (8 responses). Lessons written by the same small model at low effort.
agent_relevance: Gap 5 partly: the lesson line (S9) is not shown to beat simply re-reading the failed attempt, and effects of 7 to 10 points need 100+ tasks to confirm. Our own test must be sized for that or stay descriptive.

source: EvoCUE: learned control-program updates tested at a matched checkpoint (arXiv 2609.34988)
finding: Instead of storing lessons as text, the agent's control flow got one learned instruction at the recurring completion decision, accepted only after paired held-out confirmation. Large gains on AppWorld, no update accepted in six other domains.
numbers: deepseek-v4-flash, temperature 0. AppWorld Test-Normal n=168: 13.7% to 79.2% (110 improved, 0 regressed). Test-Challenge n=417: 6.7% to 70.0% (270 improved, 6 regressed). Same instruction attached at first step solved 5 of 16 dev tasks, at the recurring step 14. PAST-Bench pilot 0.608 to 0.772; unseen families 0.305 to 0.332 (frozen). One far-transfer task fell 0.796 to 0.510. GEPA, AFlow, AWM, MaAS at most +4.8 points.
limits: Author-run baselines are not reproductions and the baseline table columns look misaligned. Single model. One instruction fixed a failure that was mostly a premature-completion habit; not general.
agent_relevance: Where a lesson sits matters more than its wording: attach it to the state where the error recurs. Fits S9 lesson routed to the state it applies to, and held-out confirmation before keeping it.

source: EDV: Execute-Distill-Verify and the self-confirmation trap (arXiv 2606.24428)
finding: Self-written lessons often store the agent's own execution errors as advice. A separate distiller plus unanimous review by other executors cut that trap rate and raised pass@1.
numbers: tau2-bench pass@1 averages: no memory 76.4, direct self-reflection 77.7, RB-MaTTS 82.3, EDV 86.6 (Airline 72.0, Retail 88.6, Telecom 99.1). Trap rate on annotated Retail subset: self-reflection 22.0%, ReasoningBank 16.0%, RB-MaTTS 11.0%, EDV 5.0%. Paired interventions on retrieved bad lessons (60 runs per condition): target-error recurrence 50% original, 30% removed, 20% corrected; success 40%, 55%, 65%. Held-out two-fold: EDV 85.1 vs 81.1 vs 76.4. Evaluation tokens 11.2% lower.
limits: No significance tests; 60-run intervention is descriptive; reviewers can share errors; frozen memory only; pass@1 not pass^k.
agent_relevance: Supports a gate before S9 writes a lesson: unverified lessons are a source of repeated error (50% recurrence when a bad lesson is retrieved). Bears on gap 5.

source: Anchor: test memory at its source decision before storing it (arXiv 2611.10382)
finding: Only memories that shift the action in a direction that supports the source outcome are kept. Verified memory far outperformed writing every candidate.
numbers: ALFWorld 402 held-out tasks, Qwen3.5-27B: ReAct 61.19%, write-all 73.38%, magnitude test 74.88%, full Anchor 96.27% (+21.39 over magnitude only). Qwen2.5-14B Anchor 87.06% vs best baseline 72.64%. WebShop 73.50 vs 62.74. Dropping failure corrections 86.82%, dropping success reinforcement 83.83%. 41% fewer stored cards.
limits: Needs token log probabilities. Only ALFWorld and WebShop, two backbones, authors' own runs of 10 baselines. Last 70k characters not read.
agent_relevance: Failure-derived lessons contribute (about 9 points of 96 in this ablation) but need a check; consistent with d06 and d08. Not usable through a closed API without logprobs.

finding: Blind three-round self-correction lowered accuracy for 4 of 5 non-thinking models. Reasoning ('thinking') models were not run in this mode, so the question for reasoning models is still open here.
numbers: 1,340 college materials-science problems. Self-correction: Claude-Sonnet-3.7 62.54 to 61.27, DeepSeek-V3 67.02 to 62.83, GPT-4.1 68.49 to 67.32, Kimi-K2 68.78 to 66.93, Llama-4-Maverick 67.41 to 67.71. Over five models 342 answers worsened, 233 improved, net -2.1%. Cause of harm: false problem identification 69.6%, rounding over-correction 8.7%. Degradation by difficulty: easy -2.6%, medium -1.8%, hard -1.1%. Tool use (code) raised 4 of 5 models, e.g. Llama-4 67.41 to 70.15.
limits: Domain-specific, non-thinking models only, generic review prompt.
agent_relevance: Reinforces d02 and d03: harm comes from inventing a fault in a correct answer. A revise step needs evidence of a fault; executing code helped where self-critique did not (S4 test before S5).

source: Barres et al. (2025) tau2-bench dual-control agents (arXiv 2506.07982)
finding: pass^k keeps falling as k rises, more steeply in the hardest domain. Making the user share control of the environment cut pass^1 sharply.
numbers: gpt-4.1 pass^1 74% retail, 56% airline, 34% telecom; claude-3.7-sonnet telecom 49%; gpt-4.1-mini and o4-mini about 50% telecom. Moving from no-user to guided-user: pass^1 drop 18% (gpt-4.1) and 25% (o4-mini). Figure text suggests retail pass^k falling from about 0.74 at k=1 to about 0.53 at k=4 (garbled extraction, approximate).
limits: Figure values read from extracted figure text and approximate. Simulated user. Compares models, not scaffolds.
agent_relevance: Gap 2 stays open: no source opened tests a thinking scaffold with pass^k at equal tokens. EDV (d08) and EvoCUE (d07) report pass@1 or success only. Our test must report pass^k from at least 4 repeats per item.

finding: Memory distilled from both successes and failures raised success and cut interaction steps, with the paper stating larger step savings on successful cases.
numbers: WebArena success +8.3, +7.2, +4.6 points over no-memory across three backbones; up to 20% relative. Step reduction up to 2.1 fewer steps (26.9% relative) on successful cases. No-memory baseline 17.1% on a compact-model setting in the appendix, ReasoningBank 24.1%. Success and failure labels come from an LLM judge.
limits: Table text garbled in extraction; judge noise acknowledged; authors did not compare episodic or hierarchical memory designs.
agent_relevance: Failure-derived text lessons help in a published benchmark with a judge-labelled signal; consistent with S9 but dependent on a reliable success signal.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion, full text (arXiv 2303.11366)
finding: Verbal reflection across trials solved nearly all AlfWorld tasks but did not help on WebShop, where escaping a bad search habit needs varied exploration.
numbers: AlfWorld: ReAct plus Reflexion completed 130 of 134 tasks over 12 trials; ReAct-only plateaued between trials 6 and 7 with a hallucination rate near 22%. Headline: +22% AlfWorld, +20% HotPotQA, +11% HumanEval; HumanEval pass@1 91% vs 80% GPT-4. WebShop (100 environments): stopped after 4 trials with no improvement; reflections were not helpful.
limits: Needs a clean binary success signal between trials; WebShop failure is the documented boundary. Memory truncated to last 3 reflections.
agent_relevance: Upgrades the earlier abstract-level Reflexion line. Boundary: a lesson cannot create a strategy the agent never tries; an impasse needs a changed operator, not only a note.

source: Woods (2018) The theory of graceful extensibility (Environment Systems and Decisions)
finding: Could not be opened: the publisher page redirects to a login and Semantic Scholar lists the open-access status as CLOSED (169 citations). Gap 7 stays open for the primary text.
numbers: None read. Semantic Scholar metadata only: 169 citations, abstract elided by the publisher.
limits: Not opened; do not cite content from this line beyond that it is closed access.
agent_relevance: Founding-source claims remain tied to citing papers (Moerman et al., a06). Testable timing predictions for decompensation not checked.

source: Sentry held-out transfer and playbook exposure (arXiv 2610.02994, Tables 2 and 4)
finding: Lessons learned on 50 tasks transferred to 50 disjoint tasks. Putting the whole playbook in the agent's context was worse than retrieving a lesson only when a failure fires.
numbers: Held-out WebShop reward: no playbook 0.251, frozen playbook 0.364, frozen playbook always in context 0.296, full Sentry 0.495. Mind2Web Replay: 0.533, 0.651, 0.599, 0.729. Reflexion 0.295 / 0.531, ACE 0.335 / 0.562, ReasoningBank 0.250 / 0.483 versus Sentry 0.495 / 0.729. Removing always-on failure lessons from ACE raised WebShop 0.335 to 0.391.
limits: 5 runs, authors' setup, Qwen3.5-9B, same model for agent and verifier.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: yes for held-out transfer in one study, and lessons work better pulled when the failure pattern fires than kept in context. Fits S9 as a lookup at S6, not a standing prompt.

source: Sentry trigger effect on output (arXiv 2610.02994, local recovery and human audit)
finding: On whether the trigger changes output: a failure-triggered intervention gave paired local recovery of 60.5% against 33.5% without it, and 85.8% of 113 issued interventions were judged locally helpful.
numbers: 200 paired forks: 33.5% vs 60.5% recovered. Human audit of 113 interventions: 85.8% locally helpful. Over-triggering lowered reward (d05). Fire rates per failure type were not reported.
limits: How early the detector fires is not reported, which is what gap 1 asks.
agent_relevance: Gap 1 stays open: change rate is evidenced (about +27 points on forks), early firing is not. We still need a fire-time histogram from our own traces.

source: Cross-check of Gap 4: blind review on newer reasoning models
finding: No paper opened this session tests blind self-review on frontier reasoning models. Tests cover older chat models (d02, d10) or 3B to 120B open models (d03). Gap 4 stays open for 2026 reasoning models.
numbers: d10: net -2.1% over five non-thinking models. d03: single self-verification breaks 10.9% of correct answers. d02: DeepSeek-Chat at 94.0% fixes only 16.7% of its own errors.
limits: Search budget ran out before a targeted search for reasoning-model results; earlier abstract-level lines (Liu and Meng 2026, +0.6 points for one model) stand unverified.
agent_relevance: Keep S5 gated by a located failure; run our own check on the nano loop.
